title: How U.S. controls flow of advanced tech, chip, and compute to China | Explained
summary: The U.S. Commerce Department on November 16 issued an interim final rule barring data centre operators outside the U.S. equipped with advanced American AI chips from providing cloud service to businesses in two dozen countries, including China, Iran, and Russia
llm_summary: The U.S. Commerce Department just rolled out an interim rule that stops data‑center operators located outside the United States—if they’re using advanced American AI chips—from offering cloud services to customers in about 24 countries, among them China, Iran and Russia.
